title: Token-waterfall rendezvous and predictive kernel-hint scheduler for multi-GPU prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Multigpu prefill/decode workloads hit long tail latency and inefficient NCCL bursts when model kernels switch frequently or when global rendezvous barriers create idle time. Current conductor is a coarse barrier-based rendezvous which forces all ranks to align, causing bandwidth spikes and suboptimal kernel choice for heterogeneous batches.

Proposal: Implement a token-waterfall rendezvous scheduler combined with a predictive kernel-hint table. The scheduler opens asynchronous, topology-aware rendezvous windows per logical stage so token groups can flow downstream in a waterfall (staggered) pattern. Concurrently, the runtime maintains a lightweight per-workload kernel-hint table keyed by short sequence-length histograms and attention-density estimates (sparsity), allowing rank-local early kernel selection to reduce expensive kernel negotiation during handoffs. Adaptive NCCL window sizing will be used to allow overlap of point-to-point bulk transfers with compute on other ranks.

Goals: 1) Reduce p99 decode latency by >= 20% on mixed sequence workloads. 2) Reduce NCCL microburst bandwidth utilization variance by >= 30%. 3) Keep kernel misprediction rate < 5% for common workloads. 4) Maintain KV-cache correctness and deterministic outputs under staggered handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prefill+decode p99 reduced by >=20% on mixed-length benchmark suite compared to master
NCCL instantaneous bandwidth variance reduced by >=30% on corridor tests
Kernel hint misprediction <5% on production prompt sample set
Automated correctness test pass (KV cache parity) across 128 simulated requests with randomized stagger windows
Feature gated behind runtime flag and e2e rollout plan validated in dedicated cluster
rollout_plan: Deploy to dedicated staging cluster (3x A100) and run synthetic mixed-length benchmark suite
Canary to 5% Dedicated capacity with realtime telemetry monitoring for 24h
If no regressions, 25% for 48h then 100% on non-critical tenants
Full rollout requires sign-off from performance and reliability teams
comments: 2026-02-14: Spike completed. Prototype shows reduced alignment idle time by ~18% on uniform batches. -- Marco
2026-02-21: Design review notes: add per-topology backpressure to avoid token pileup on slow links. Action: add credit-based limiter in scheduler. -- Priya (Perf)
2026-02-28: Implemented kernel-hint table. Using a tiny LRU keyed by (seq_len_bucket, attn_density_bucket). Initial hit rate 78% on sampled traces. Need to tune buckets. -- Marco
2026-03-03: Discovered GC pause interaction on Python-based conductor tests leading to false handoff timings. Workaround: move time-sensitive path to C++ worker shim. -- Aisha

2026-03-07: Telemetry shows NCCL peak smoothing improved but occasional 2x bursts on hetero-device tests. Hypothesis: hint mispred on long tails causes rebinds. Plan: add confidence score and conservative fallback to barrier when confidence < threshold. -- Marco
2026-03-10: Integration tests added (kv-cache-parity, randomized-stagger). All pass locally. Preparing perf run on staging cluster tomorrow. -- Aisha
test_plan: Unit tests for kernel-hint table eviction and serialization
Integration tests: kv-cache parity with staggered handoffs (deterministic seed)
Perf harness: mixed-length benchmark (short/med/long ratio 50/30/20) across 4-node mp setup
Fault injection: drop handshake messages, simulate slow link, induce NCCL retry to validate graceful fallback
Canary observability playbook and automatic rollback on p99 regression
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Kernel misprediction leads to runtime rebinds and higher latency. Mitigation: conservative confidence thresholds and quick rollback path to global barrier.
Risk: Staggered handoffs complicate KV cache consistency. Mitigation: versioned cache tokens and deterministic apply order in handoff messages.
Risk: NCCL tuning parameters may be hardware dependent. Mitigation: expose tunables per-device-type and collect device-level telemetry during canary.
Risk: Increased code complexity in conductor. Mitigation: keep feature gated and add thorough unit/integration coverage with clear invariants documented.
